Title: Scared of heights? Go anyway!

Staff: 5 stars | Safety: 5 stars | Price: 3 stars | Facilities: 4 stars

I booked the Saturday morning Beginners' Taster at Clip In Climbing with two classmates, mainly because I am terrified of heights and wanted to prove something to myself. Ninety minutes later, I had reached the top of the yellow wall three times.

Our instructor, Mandy, earns the five stars for staff. She learnt all six of our names in the first minute and never once made the slower climbers feel like a nuisance. Safety gets full marks too: the safety talk was short but clear, she checked every harness twice, and the auto-belay lowered me so gently that I actually started to enjoy coming down.

Price is where the gym loses points. Even at the student rate, $180 is a lot for an hour and a half, although shoe and harness hire are included. The facilities are good – clean changing rooms, proper lockers and a water refill station – but the rest area is tiny and was packed by the time our session finished.

If you are a complete beginner, or you want something more active than karaoke for a weekend with friends, this is the place. My one suggestion: offer a shorter, cheaper session so that students can come back more often. I would be first in the queue.

Reviewed by Chris Wong

commentary.content: All three points are fully covered. The session is described through specific moments, each of the four ratings is justified (the instructor's attention, the harness checks, the price weighed against what is included, the crowded rest area), and the improvement follows naturally from the price comment. The recommendation names a clear type of visitor.
commentary.language: Accurate and varied sentences with a natural review voice (Price is where the gym loses points; I would be first in the queue). Vocabulary is precise without being showy. A few sentences are fairly simple, which keeps it at 6 rather than 7.
commentary.organisation: An engaging title and opening, a logical move from the session to the ratings to the recommendation, and a punchy ending. Paragraphs are short and focused, exactly right for a website review.

Title: A good place for beginners

Staff: 4 stars, Safety: 5 stars, Price: 2 stars, Facilities: 4 stars

Last Sunday I went to Clip In Climbing in Kwun Tong with my cousin. We joined the Beginners' Taster Session. It was 90 minutes and there were six people in our group.

First, the staff are very friendly. Our instructor explained the safety rules clearly and he helped us to wear the harness. However, sometimes he talked to his friend and did not watch us. So I gave only 4 stars.

About safety, I think it is very safe. Every climber must listen the safety talk before climb and the walls have auto-belay, so even you fall down you will not get hurt.

The price is quite expensive. I am a student so I paid $180, but it is still too much for students. The facilities is good. There are lockers, changing rooms and a water refill station, it is very convenient.

In conclusion, I will recommend this gym to people who want to try something new. I hope the gym can give more discount for students. Overall, it is a good experience.

commentary.content: All three points are addressed and each rating has a reason, so the task is mostly achieved. However, the session itself is described only in general terms, the reasons for Price and Facilities are brief or partly copied from the advertisement, and 'people who want to try something new' is a vague recommendation. More vivid, personal detail would be needed for 6.
commentary.language: Simple sentences are generally accurate, but there are errors with prepositions, verb forms and agreement (listen the safety talk before climb; The facilities is good) and a comma splice. Vocabulary is plain (very friendly, very convenient) and 'In conclusion' does not suit a review. Complex sentences would need to be more reliable for 5.
commentary.organisation: Paragraphs follow the content points, but linking is mechanical (First, About safety, In conclusion) and the review ends with a formula rather than a verdict. The order is clear but reads like a checklist.

samples.text:
Staying Home Is Not Standing Still

My cousin Ivan is twenty-seven, has a steady job as a civil engineer, and still sleeps in the bedroom he has had since primary school. A decade ago, his friends might have mocked him. Today, half of them are doing exactly the same. Living with one's parents well into adulthood has become the norm in Hong Kong. It is easy to dismiss these young people as lazy, but I believe that, for most of them, it is a sensible decision.

The main reason is simple: housing. Renting even a tiny flat can swallow a large share of a new graduate's salary, and buying one is out of the question for years. Public housing is an option, but applicants often wait several years. On top of this, many young people now postpone full-time work to take a master's degree, and their first jobs are often short-term contracts with little job security. Moving out in these circumstances would mean living from one payday to the next.

Staying at home, by contrast, gives young adults room to plan and to accumulate savings. Ivan pays his parents a fixed sum every month, yet he still manages to save around a third of his income. Within five years he expects to have a deposit for a flat of his own, without borrowing from anyone. His friends who rent hand that same money to a landlord and have little to show for it.

There is also a family benefit that is often overlooked. Many Hong Kong parents are approaching retirement just as their children start work. When adult children live at home, they can accompany a parent to medical appointments, fix the Wi-Fi or simply share dinner. In a city with a rapidly ageing population, this kind of everyday support is vital rather than trivial.

Critics argue that staying at home delays independence: young people who have never paid a gas bill or cooked for themselves will struggle to cope later. This is a fair concern, but it confuses independence with an address. A twenty-five-year-old who contributes to the household budget, does their share of the housework and has a clear plan for moving out is far more independent than one who rents a flat on borrowed money.

Staying at home, then, is a smart and pragmatic choice when it is a choice with a purpose. Young people should treat it as a temporary stage with clear priorities, not a hiding place: pay their way, pull their weight and set a date. Done like this, a few extra years under the family roof is not standing still at all – it is building a foundation.

commentary.content: Fully meets the task. The reasons (housing costs, public housing waiting time, longer study, short-term contracts) are explained in a Hong Kong context, the stance is clear from the first paragraph, and it is argued with developed points on saving and family support. The counter-argument is answered convincingly, and the conditions in the conclusion show mature, original thinking. The cousin's example is used as evidence, not as a story.
commentary.language: A wide range of accurate structures (concession, contrast, conditionals) and precise vocabulary (deposit, postpone, pull their weight, contributes to the household budget). The tone is formal but readable for magazine readers. A few phrases are slightly conversational (fix the Wi-Fi), which keeps it at 6.
commentary.organisation: Clear thesis, logical movement from causes to benefits to rebuttal, and a conclusion that echoes the title. Topic sentences are strong and linking is varied (by contrast, On top of this, then). The two benefit paragraphs could be connected more explicitly for 7.

Staying at Home for Longer

Nowadays, many young people in Hong Kong live with their parents until they are almost thirty years old. Some people think they are lazy, but I think staying at home is a smart choice for young people. In this essay, I will explain the reasons why this is happening and why it is smart.

First of all, the most important reason is the price of flats in Hong Kong is very high. Everyone knows that Hong Kong flats are the most expensive in the world. A young people who just graduated from university do not have enough money to rent a flat. Therefore, they prefer to live with their parents.

Moreover, many young people need to study more after university. For example, my sister is studying a master degree now and she does not have full-time job. So she still lives in our home.

Furthermore, Hong Kong people think family is very important. Many parents also want their children to live with them because they will feel lonely. My grandmother always says a family should eat dinner together every night.

I think staying at home is smart because young people can save a lot of money. They can use the money to buy a flat in the future or travel to other countries. Besides, they can take care of their parents when they become old. This is good for both of them.

However, living with parents also have many disadvantages. Young people will lose their privacy and they cannot bring friends home. Sometimes they will quarrel with their parents about small things, for example what time to go home. Also, they will become not independent because their mother cook and wash clothes for them. When they get married, they will not know how to take care of their own family. So young people should learn to live alone when they have chance.

In conclusion, there are many reasons why young people in Hong Kong live with their parents for longer, such as the high price of flats, study more and the family culture. Every coin has two sides. I think it is a smart choice for young people because they can save money and take care of their parents.

commentary.content: Both parts of the task are attempted: three reasons are given and a stance is stated. However, the reasons are only asserted (Everyone knows that Hong Kong flats are the most expensive in the world; my sister is studying) with little explanation, the grandmother example is not about young adults' choices, and the case for 'smart' is one short paragraph. The disadvantages paragraph drifts away from the stance and even ends by telling young people to live alone, which is never answered. The essay just meets the task.
commentary.language: Simple sentences are generally accurate, but complex structures often go wrong (the most important reason is the price of flats … is very high; will become not independent) and there are frequent agreement and article errors (A young people … do not have; living with parents also have; their mother cook; does not have full-time job). Vocabulary is adequate but repetitive (smart, very important) and 'Every coin has two sides' is a cliché.
commentary.organisation: Clear paragraphs with topic sentences, so the essay is easy to follow. Linking is mechanical (First of all, Moreover, Furthermore, Besides, However), the disadvantages paragraph is not linked back to the argument, and the conclusion is formulaic: it repeats the introduction and adds a cliché.

samples.text:
Dear Ms Fong,

I am writing to apply for the post of Summer Guide at the Hillcrest Museum of Childhood, which I saw advertised on your website last week. I am seventeen years old and have just completed Secondary 5 at Silver Creek Secondary School. I believe my experience with young children and my interest in Hong Kong's past make me a suitable candidate.

For the past two years, I have volunteered every Friday afternoon as a reading buddy for Primary 2 pupils at a primary school near my home. This has taught me that young children listen best when they are asked questions rather than given a lecture. I have also learnt how to keep a group of ten excited seven-year-olds together, which I imagine is a useful skill in a busy gallery. Last summer, I worked as a helper at a day camp run by our local community centre, where I led games and made sure every child was collected safely at the end of the day.

Your new gallery interests me personally. Last year, for a school history project, I interviewed several elderly residents in my estate about the games they played as children. They described hopscotch chalked on the pavement, marbles, and paper dolls bought for a few cents, and I was struck by how much fun they had with so little. I would love the chance to pass these stories on to children who have grown up with tablets. For example, I could ask each group to guess what an old toy was used for before revealing the answer, or, if space allows, let them try a simple street game themselves.

In addition, I speak fluent Cantonese and English and can get by in Putonghua, so I would be able to guide groups from different types of schools. I hold a basic first aid certificate, which I hope would reassure teachers bringing young pupils to the museum, and I am available from Monday to Saturday throughout July and August. I am punctual and used to following instructions carefully, since my volunteer work requires me to sign children in and out on time.

I have enclosed my CV and a reference from my class teacher, Mr Tsang. I would be very happy to attend an interview at any time convenient to you. Thank you for considering my application, and I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours sincerely,
Chris Wong

commentary.content: All the expected areas are covered with credible, concrete evidence: reading-buddy work and day-camp experience are linked to the demands of guiding children, and the oral history project gives a genuine connection to the gallery. The ideas for engaging young visitors show initiative. Slightly more on why the writer wants this particular job, beyond the history project, would make the content complete.
commentary.language: Accurate, varied and assured throughout (which I imagine is a useful skill in a busy gallery; I was struck by how much fun they had with so little). Vocabulary is precise and the formal register is consistent from salutation to sign-off.
commentary.organisation: Purpose is stated at once, each body paragraph focuses on one area of suitability, transitions are smooth, and the layout and closing are fully correct for a letter to a named person.

Dear Ms Fong,

I am Chris Wong, a Form 5 student from Silver Creek Secondary School. I am writing this letter to apply the job of summer guide in your museum. I saw the advertisement on the internet and I am very interesting in this job.

Firstly, I like children very much. I think children are very cute and lovely, and I always enjoy to play with them. I have experience to work with children. Last year, I was a tutor of my neighbour's son and I taught him English and Maths. I was very patient with him and his result become better. So I think I can get along with children well.

Secondly, I am interested in history. I think history is very important because we can learn many things from the past. When I was small, my grandmother told me some stories about the old days and I found them very interesting. I want to let more children know about the old Hong Kong. Nowadays children only play with mobile phones, they do not know the traditional games. I believe they will be very excited because they never see these toys before.

Moreover, I have good communication skills. I am a member of the English Society in my school and I sometimes help in activities. I can speak Cantonese and English, so I can communicate the children. Also, I am a friendly person and children like to talk with me, it is because I like children and I always smile to them.

Furthermore, I am a responsible and hard-working person. I am never late for school and I always finish my homework on time. I am also willing to learn new things. I am free in the whole summer holiday and I can work from Monday to Friday.

In conclusion, I am suitable for this job because I like children, I am interested in history and I have good communication skills. I will try my best to do this job well if you give me this chance.

If you have any question, please contact me by phone or email. Thank you for your time and I am looking forward to your reply.

Yours faithfully,
Chris Wong

commentary.content: The letter applies for the job and covers experience, interest and availability, so it is broadly relevant. However, most points are generic claims (I like children; history is very important; I am responsible and hard-working) with little specific evidence, the 'I like children' point is repeated three times, and the link to guiding groups in a toy gallery is weak: there is no idea of how the writer would lead or explain to children, and being on time for school is not relevant evidence. Only the tutoring example is partly developed.
commentary.language: Simple sentences are mostly accurate, but there are frequent errors with prepositions, verb patterns and tenses (apply the job; interesting in; enjoy to play; experience to work; communicate the children; his result become better; they never see), comma splices, and a sweeping generalisation. Vocabulary is plain and repetitive (very interesting, very cute, very important).
commentary.organisation: Clear letter layout and one paragraph per point, so the letter is easy to follow. However, linking is mechanical (Firstly, Secondly, Moreover, Furthermore, In conclusion), the conclusion simply lists the three points again in essay style, and 'Yours faithfully' does not match 'Dear Ms Fong'.

Dear Sir,

My name is Chris Wong. I am 16 years old and I am Form 5 student. My school is Silver Creek Secondary School. I want to apply the summer job of museum guide. I see your advertisement on the internet and my mother tell me to apply.

I like children very much. I have a little sister, she is 8 years old, I always play with her and take care her when my parents are busy. So I think I can take care the children in the museum. Children is very cute and I am very patient.

I also like museum. I went to many museum in Hong Kong before with my school and my family. The toy in your museum is very old and special, I want to know more about them. I think it is very fun.

I am a hard working person and I never late. I also good at English, I get B in my last exam. I can work in July and August but not on Sunday because I need to go to tuition class.

I hope you will give me the job, I promise I will do my best. Please reply me as soon as possible.

Availability is given, but the letter offers little evidence that would persuade an employer.
commentary.language: Frequent basic errors (take care her; Children is very cute; many museum; I never late) and several comma splices. commentary.organisation: Short paragraphs with one idea each, but the ideas are listed without development or linking. The layout is wrong for a letter to a named person: 'Dear Sir', 'Best wishes' and a first name only.

samples.text:
To: The Student Council
From: Chris Wong, 5C (Library Prefect)
Date: 20 November
Subject: Use of the school library after school

1. Introduction
Since September the library has stayed open until 6.30 pm on weekdays. This report sets out how students have been using the extra hours and suggests ways to maximise their value.

2. Method
Between 3 and 14 November I counted the students in the library every half hour from 4 pm to 6.30 pm and noted what they were doing. I also gave a one-page questionnaire to two classes in each form; 214 students returned it. In addition, I spoke informally to the librarian about borrowing records and peak times.

3. Findings
3.1 Who uses the library
Attendance is considerably higher than expected but uneven. On an average day about 60 students were present at 4.30 pm, but fewer than 15 remained after 5.30 pm. Senior students made up nearly three quarters of regular users; only one in ten junior respondents had stayed after school more than once.

3.2 What students do there
Most users come to do homework or revise, usually in groups. Very few borrow books: the counter recorded an average of six loans per evening. The six computers were occupied almost continuously, and several students were seen waiting over twenty minutes to print.

3.3 Problems
Three issues were evident. First, noise: group discussions at the large tables made it hard for others to concentrate, and 41% of respondents named noise as their main complaint. Second, junior students said they felt "out of place" among seniors. Third, many students leave early because they are hungry and food is not allowed.

4. Recommendations
4.1 Divide the library into two zones: a silent area near the bookshelves and a discussion area at the large tables, marked with simple signs.
4.2 Run a weekly "Junior Hour" from 4 to 5 pm on Wednesdays, with book clubs or homework help from senior prefects, to make the library more welcoming to Forms 1 to 3.
4.3 Introduce a booking sheet for the computers and printer so that time is not wasted queuing.
4.4 Ask the school to consider allowing light snacks in the corridor outside the library between 5 and 5.15 pm.

5. Conclusion
The longer opening hours are clearly valued, especially by senior students preparing for examinations. With a few inexpensive adjustments, the library could serve a wider range of students and keep them there for longer. I would be happy to present these findings at the next Student Council meeting.

commentary.content: Fully meets the task. The method is clear and believable, findings cover who uses the library, what they do and the problems, supported by specific figures, and each recommendation matches a finding. The survey figures are invented, which is acceptable in the exam, but the App should not present them as facts.
commentary.language: Concise, objective and accurate, with a good range of reporting structures (fewer than 15 remained; made up nearly three quarters; were seen waiting). Vocabulary is precise and well suited to a report. Sentences are deliberately plain, so the range is wide rather than very wide.
commentary.organisation: Complete report layout with a memo header, logical numbered headings and sub-points. Recommendations are clearly linked to findings, and the conclusion is brief and forward-looking.

samples.text:
Report on Students Using the Library After School

Introduction
The purpose of this report is to find out how students use the library after school. Since this school year, the library opens until 6:30 pm from Monday to Friday. I did a survey to 100 students and I also went to the library for two weeks to observe.

Findings
According to the survey, most of students go to the library after school to do homework and revise for tests. They said the library is quiet and comfortable, and there are air-conditioner, so it is better than study at home. Also, some students go to the library because they need to wait for their parents to pick them up or wait for tutorial class.

However, I found that some students do not use the library properly. Some students play mobile games and some chat loudly with their friends. This make other students cannot concentrate. Also, some students use the computers to watch videos, so other students who need to do their projects cannot use them.

Besides, most students leave the library at around 5:30 pm because they are hungry and they cannot eat inside. Only a few students stay until it close.

Moreover, I discovered that not many students borrow books. Most of the students only use the library as a study room. This is a waste because there are many good books in the library.

Recommendations
Firstly, the school should make more rules for the library. For example, students cannot play games or talk loudly. If they break the rules, the librarian should ask them to leave.

Secondly, the school should limit the time of using computers. Each student can only use the computer for 30 minutes so everyone can have a chance.

Thirdly, the school can encourage students to borrow more books by holding some reading activities.

Conclusion
To conclude, many students use the library after school and it is very useful for them. However, there are still some problems. I hope the Student Council will consider my suggestions to make the library better.

commentary.content: Purpose, findings and recommendations are all present, so the task is met. However, the findings are general (most of students, some students) with no figures from the survey or observation, little is said about when students come or how long they stay, and the recommendations are general (make more rules, hold some reading activities) and addressed to the school rather than the Council.
commentary.language: Simple reporting sentences are mostly accurate, but there are errors in tense, articles and word form (the library opens until; most of students; better than study at home) and Chinese-influenced structures (This make other students cannot concentrate). Vocabulary is adequate but plain.
commentary.organisation: Headings are used and each section has a clear focus, but the To/From/Date/Subject block is missing and linking is mechanical (Also, However, Moreover, Firstly, Secondly, Thirdly). Recommendations are not clearly matched to individual findings.

Dear Student Council,

I am Chris Wong from 4B. You ask me to find out how students use library after school. So I do a survey and look at the library two weeks.

I find that many student go to library after school. They go there to do homework, because at home they have many distraction, like TV and computer games. In library is more quiet. But some student is very noisy, they talk and laugh loudly and the librarian don't say anything. I think this is very unfair to other student.

Also the computer is not enough. There are only few computer and always have people use. I want to print my notes but I wait very long time.

Many students don't borrow book because they think reading is boring, they like to watch videos online more. I think school should buy more comic book and magazine so student will like to borrow.

I think the library is very good place, I like to go there everyday. The school should open the library until 8 pm so we can study more longer. Also the school should let us eat in the library because we are very hungry after school.

Hope you can accept my suggestions.
Thank you.

Chris Wong

commentary.content: Partly meets the task. Some findings are given (homework, noise, too few computers, few loans), but they are mixed with personal opinions and the writer's own experience; the survey is mentioned but never used. Recommendations are given, though one (opening until 8 pm) does not follow from any finding.
commentary.language: Short simple sentences are generally understandable, but errors are frequent in tense, agreement and plurals (So I do a survey; some student is very noisy; the librarian don't) and some structures obscure meaning (There are only few computer and always have people use). Vocabulary is simple and the tone personal.
commentary.organisation: Written as a letter, with no report headings or sections; findings, opinions and suggestions run into each other, and the ending is abrupt. There is some paragraphing and simple linking (Also, But).

samples.text:
Weekend Zero: How I Won $50 by Spending $0

Last Thursday, my best friend Ryan watched me buy my third bubble tea of the week and laughed. "You couldn't last one weekend without spending money," he said. "Fifty dollars says you can't." Naturally, I shook his hand. Here's how it went.

The rules
We agreed on three: no buying anything, no borrowing money, and no asking my parents to pay for things I'd normally buy myself. Meals at home were allowed – I'm stubborn, not crazy.

Saturday: the hard part
I hadn't realised how much of my routine costs money until I couldn't spend any. My usual Saturday is simple: train to Mong Kok, lunch with friends, a bit of shopping. This time I deliberately left my wallet at home and couldn't even take the bus, so I walked forty minutes to meet everyone at the park, with a sandwich and a bottle of water in my bag.

The real test came at three o'clock, when the whole group queued up for bubble tea. I stood there clutching my water bottle while they debated sugar levels. I was tempted, I'll admit; resisting was the longest ten minutes of my life. But then something funny happened. Because I didn't have a drink to hold, I was the one who suggested kicking a ball around on the grass, and we ended up playing until it got dark. Nobody even mentioned shopping.

Sunday: the surprise
On Sunday I woke up with no plans and, for once, no budget for any. I spontaneously dug out an old jigsaw puzzle, spent the afternoon finishing it with my little brother, and then went for a run along the waterfront with my dad. It was the first weekend in months that I hadn't scrolled through online shops on my phone.

What I learnt
By Sunday night I had spent exactly $0 and won the bet, and I felt a satisfaction no shopping trip has ever given me. More importantly, I realised that most of my spending isn't really about wanting things – it's about habit, impulse and boredom. The bubble tea was never the point; being with my friends was, and that turned out to be free.

Will I give up shopping forever? Definitely not. But I've decided to make a no-spend weekend a monthly ritual and put the money I save towards a new camera.

Ryan reluctantly admitted defeat on Monday morning, but I'm still waiting for my fifty dollars.

Have you ever tried a no-spend challenge? Tell me how you survived in the comments!

commentary.content: A vivid, well-shaped story that covers every part of the task: the bet is set up with dialogue, the rules are clear, temptations are concrete (transport, bubble tea) and solved inventively, the result is given, and the reflection on habit and boredom is personal and genuinely insightful. A strong sense of blog readers throughout.
commentary.language: Natural, varied sentences with a convincing conversational voice; narrative tenses, including the past perfect, are accurate; word choice is lively without forced idioms (I'm stubborn, not crazy; for once, no budget for any).
commentary.organisation: Engaging title and opening, sub-headings that guide readers through the weekend, and an ending that links back to the bet and invites comments. The 'The rules' section is a little brief compared with the rest, which keeps it at 6.

samples.text:
My No Money Weekend

Hi everyone! Nowadays, many teenagers in Hong Kong spend too much money on food and entertainment, and I am one of them. Last week my friend Kelvin said I cannot live one weekend without spending any money. He bet me 100 dollars. I think it is easy, so I said yes.

First, on Saturday morning I woke up at 10 am. Usually I will go to the cafe near my home to eat breakfast, but this time I ate bread at home. It is not as delicious as the cafe but it is OK. Then, I want to go to see my friends in Causeway Bay, but I need to take the bus and it costs money. So I stayed at home and watched TV with my sister. After that, I played mobile games in my room. After that, I had lunch with my family. The time passed very slowly and I felt very boring. In the afternoon, my friends sent me a message and ask me to go to the cinema. I really wanted to go because it was a new movie I was waiting for a long time. Although I wanted to go very much, but I remembered the bet, so I refused them. I felt very sad and I almost gave up. At night, my friends post many photos of the movie and the popcorn online and I feel very jealous.

Then, on Sunday, I decided to go hiking with my father. We walked to a hill near our home, it was free. The view was very beautiful and we discussed about my school life on the way.

After that, we went home and I did my homework. At night, my mother cooked my favourite food, so I don't need to spend money to buy any snacks. Finally, I won the bet! Kelvin need to give me 100 dollars. I was very happy.

In conclusion, through this experience I learnt that money is not the most important thing in our life.

Thank you for reading my blog! See you next time!

commentary.content: The task is mostly achieved: the bet, the weekend and the result are all included, and the cinema temptation is partly developed (the writer feels sad and almost gives up). However, most of the post is a list of events in time order with little reflection, the hike with the writer's father is only mentioned, and what the writer learnt is stated in one generic sentence, so the second part of the task is underdeveloped.
commentary.language: Simple sentences are mostly accurate, but tenses shift frequently between past and present (I think it is easy; I want to go; ask me to go; I don't need to) and the past perfect is not used where needed. There are also errors in word form and structure (I felt very boring; Although … but; discussed about), a comma splice, and plain, repeated vocabulary (very boring, very sad, very beautiful).
commentary.organisation: The order of events is easy to follow, but linking is mechanical (First / Then / After that / After that / Finally) and paragraphing is uneven: one very long Saturday paragraph, while Sunday is split into two short ones. The essay-style opening (Nowadays, many teenagers…) and 'In conclusion' ending sit awkwardly with the blog greeting and sign-off.

No Spend Money Weekend

Money is very important in our life. Nowadays many teenager spend too much money on snack, clothes and phone games. So we should learn how to save money.

Last weekend my friend say I cannot no spend money for two day. I say I can do it.

Saturday I stay at home all day. I play computer game and sleep. My mother cook lunch and dinner for me so I no need to buy food. It is very easy but very boring.

Sunday my friend ask me go to shopping mall. I go with them but I not buy anything. I see a very nice shoes but I can't buy it, I feel very sad. My friend buy many thing, they laugh me.

In the end I win the bet. My friend give me 50 dollars.

There are many way to save money. First, we can bring lunch box to school. Second, we can go to library to read book, no need to buy. Third, we can walk to school, not take bus. If we save money, we can buy thing we really want in the future and help our parents.

In conclusion, save money is very important for teenager. Everyone should try no spend money weekend.

commentary.content: The bet and a few events are included and the result is given, but the story is very thin and there is no real reflection on what the writer learnt. Large parts are general advice on saving money, which turns the blog into an essay.
commentary.language: Frequent errors in tense, agreement and plurals (my friend say; I not buy anything; many way) and some structures obscure meaning (I cannot no spend money). Vocabulary is very limited (very easy, very boring, very sad).
commentary.organisation: An essay-style introduction and conclusion surround a short story; the tips paragraph breaks the narrative; paragraphs are loosely connected and the blog has no sense of a reader.
